Calling episomal ecDNA

Source: vignettes/calling.Rmd
calling.Rmd

call_simple_excision() flags ecDNA amplicons most likely generated by a simple excision and re-circularisation event — an episome — rather than by a complex, breakage-driven process. For each amplicon it inspects the structural-variant breakpoints at the boundaries and applies the episome heuristic: a boundary duplication (DUP) carrying the highest variant fraction (VF), non-gained flanking segments (consistent with a circle excised from an otherwise diploid region), and a candidate deletion “excision scar”.

The example data

The package bundles a textbook episomal EGFR ecDNA on chr7 (fictional sample "EXAMPLE01"), in the AmpliconArchitect + PURPLE-style GRanges the caller expects. The data are synthetic (no patient data).

names(ex_caller_inputs)
#> [1] "ecdna_gr"        "breakpoints_gr"  "cnv_gr"          "cancer_genes_gr"

Calling 

res <- call_simple_excision(
  ecdna_gr        = ex_caller_inputs$ecdna_gr,
  breakpoints_gr  = ex_caller_inputs$breakpoints_gr,
  cnv_gr          = ex_caller_inputs$cnv_gr,
  cancer_genes_gr = ex_caller_inputs$cancer_genes_gr
)

res[, c("event", "svclass", "VF", "duplication_at_boundary",
        "episomal", "has_excision_scar")]
#>     event svclass    VF duplication_at_boundary episomal has_excision_scar
#>    <char>  <char> <num>                  <char>   <char>            <char>
#> 1:   DEL1     DEL   200                   FALSE     TRUE              TRUE
#> 2:   DUP1     DUP  1000                    TRUE     TRUE              TRUE
#> 3:   DUP1     DUP  1000                    TRUE     TRUE              TRUE
#> 4:   DEL1     DEL   200                   FALSE     TRUE              TRUE

The boundary duplications carry the highest VF in the amplicon, the flanks are diploid, and a deletion scar is present — so every breakpoint of this amplicon is classified episomal = "TRUE" with has_excision_scar = "TRUE". An amplicon with the same boundary DUP but gained flanks (i.e. not excised from a diploid region) is instead returned as episomal = "FALSE" — the discrimination the caller is built for.

Running without AmpliconArchitect

AmpliconArchitect is optional. Pass ecdna_gr = NULL and EpiTracer detects the focal-amplicon seeds directly from the copy-number segments (via detect_amplicon_seeds()), so it can run from SV + CN alone:

res2 <- call_simple_excision(
  ecdna_gr        = NULL,
  breakpoints_gr  = ex_caller_inputs$breakpoints_gr,
  cnv_gr          = ex_caller_inputs$cnv_gr,
  cancer_genes_gr = ex_caller_inputs$cancer_genes_gr
)
unique(res2$episomal)
#> [1] "TRUE"

Using your own data

The inputs mirror the columns EpiTracer expects from real pipelines: ecDNA amplicon regions from AmpliconArchitect and allele-specific SV / copy-number calls from PURPLE (Hartwig Medical Foundation pipeline). See ?call_simple_excision for the required metadata columns — SV/CN calls from any pipeline can be coerced to the same shape, and missing columns produce an explicit error.
